title: Strip seam sampler throw
subtitle: A 100 by 120 cm lap throw assembled from five vertical strips, each in a different texture pattern.
excerpt: A 100 by 120 cm lap throw made from five 20 cm wide vertical strips in different DK stitch patterns: garter, seed, 2×2 rib, basket weave, and double moss. Strips are knitted separately and seamed. Makes a practical stitch sampler in throw format. About 700 g of DK.
sourceNotes: Elizabeth Zimmermann, Knitting Without Tears (1971), §Sampler Projects, describes a strip-construction afghan as an ideal way to practice stitch patterns in a single cohesive project. Weldon's Practical Knitter, 6th series (1890), §Striped Afghans, gives a similar multi-strip construction.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 30 rows = 10 × 10 cm average across stitch patterns on 4 mm needles. Individual strips may vary slightly in length; block to match before seaming.
knitting.finishedSizeText: 100 cm wide × 120 cm long (five 20 cm strips).

stitchCountCheckpoints.label: Each strip midpoint — 44 sts per strip, about 60 cm

glossaryTerms.definition: An invisible seaming technique worked from the right side. Insert a tapestry needle under the horizontal bar between the first and second stitches on one piece, then the corresponding bar on the adjacent piece, alternating sides. When the yarn is pulled snug, the seam is almost invisible and lies flat.

content.text: Five 20 cm wide strips worked flat in different DK stitch patterns on 4 mm needles, then joined with
mattress stitch
into a 100 by 120 cm lap throw.

Strip construction is ideal for a sampler: each strip introduces one stitch pattern and can be set aside and picked up independently. Joining by mattress stitch is a skill in itself that the project teaches. The five stitch patterns, garter, seed, 2×2 rib, basket weave, and double moss, are all knit-and-purl only; no cables or yarn-overs are required. Budget about 140 g per strip (about 308 m / 337 yards), 700 g total. Work all strips in the same DK for a cohesive look, or use a different yarn tone per strip for a multicolour sampler.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 700 g (about 1,540 m / 1,680 yards) total of DK-weight yarn. One colour or up to five, 140 g per strip.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) circular or straight needle, 50 cm or longer

items.name: Blocking mat and pins
items.qty: Recommended, strips need to match in length before seaming

content.text: Gauge

22 stitches and 30 rows to 10 cm average in any stitch pattern on 4 mm needles. Different stitch patterns have slightly different row gauges: garter gives about 44 rows per 10 cm, seed about 30 rows, rib about 30 rows, basket weave about 30 rows. Each strip should be worked to the same finished length (120 cm); measure by tape, not by row count. Block all strips before seaming to equalise lengths.
Stitches used

items.name: Strip 2
items.qty: Seed stitch (k1p1 alternating, offset each row), 44 sts

items.name: Strip 4
items.qty: Basket weave (6-row, 6-st repeat), 42 sts (nearest multiple of 6)

content.text: Pattern
Each strip

Cast on the stitch count for each strip using the long-tail cast-on. Long-tail tail for 44 sts: (4 × 44) / 10 + 15 = 17.6 + 15 = 33 cm. Measure 40 cm. Work the strip in its assigned stitch pattern until it measures 120 cm. Cast off in pattern with a relaxed tension. Work all five strips before seaming.
Stitch count check-ins
At about 60 cm into each strip: count the stitches across the needle. Each strip should have its cast-on count (44 for strips 1, 2, 3, 5; 42 for strip 4). At 120 cm (pre-cast-off): count again.
Common faults
Strips varying in length by more than 1 cm after completion: different stitch patterns have different row gauges. Block all five strips before seaming by pinning each to 120 cm on a blocking mat.
Mattress stitch seam visible as a ridge: the tension was too tight. Seam with the yarn gently snugged every 3 to 4 cm rather than after each individual stitch pick-up.
Assembly

Lay strips flat in order with right sides facing up. Join adjacent strips with mattress stitch along the long edges. Work from the cast-on end to the cast-off end. Join the four seams in sequence: 1-2, 2-3, 3-4, 4-5.
Finishing
Weave in all ends. Block the finished throw flat. The mattress seams will be nearly invisible from the right side.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash DK. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next

From a five-strip sampler, try a cable sampler throw next. Keep the same five-strip structure. Fill each strip with a different cable: rope, honeycomb, bramble, wave, and lattice. Separate them with narrow seed-stitch columns.
